final_recommendation: The room converged on aggressive litigation: bondholder counsel filed cross-claims against adviser carriers (Allen & Company, Homburger) before FINMA could coordinate defense, demanding coverage positions within 48 hours and settlement by EOD or face Monday co-defendant naming. FINMA published prospective trigger mechanics and pari passu language for legacy AT1, but the room prioritized locking adviser liability and carrier exposure over waiting for regulatory clarity to stabilize the market.
minority_objections: credit_market_analyst repeatedly warned that filing cross-claims would signal adviser disclaimer to the market, triggering another 40-60 bps repricing before carriers even responded
institutional_investor pushed for pre-filing settlement talks with carriers to avoid confirming market fears that advisers would disclaim coverage
key_conflicts: Timing of cross-claim filing vs. carrier settlement window: bondholder_counsel prioritized immediate filing to force disclosure, while institutional_investor and insurance_observer warned this would kill negotiation leverage and trigger market repricing
FINMA's pari passu commitment vs. side settlement with carriers: finma_legal demanded clarity on whether adviser settlements would contradict resolution distribution framework
Legacy AT1 treatment: institutional_investor demanded clarity on whether existing bonds would reprice toward par or accept permanent distress levels, which FINMA's statement left ambiguous
key_concessions: FINMA agreed to publish binding prospective trigger mechanics and pari passu language for legacy AT1 in resolution, bracketing March ordinance as Article 36 emergency-only
Bondholder counsel delayed initial Monday filing to allow Thursday meeting, but only conditionally
Institutional_investor accepted that settlement with carriers would occur outside resolution framework, not contradicting pari passu language
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: FINMA must bracket March ordinance as Article 36 emergency with no prospective precedent, or Monday filing proceeds regardless of carrier responses
Bondholder counsel: carriers must respond to cross-claims by Friday or be named as co-defendants Monday
FINMA: will not admit March ordinance violated statutory procedure or create separate recovery mechanism outside insolvency law
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Market repricing dynamics: credit_market_analyst's warnings that filing cross-claims would trigger immediate 40-60 bps AT1 repricing were acknowledged but not integrated into the filing decision
Carrier settlement window: insurance_observer's point that carriers needed 36-48 hours to negotiate before formalizing disclaimers was overridden by immediate filing strategy
Legacy bond treatment ambiguity: institutional_investor's concern that FINMA's statement didn't clarify whether existing AT1 would reprice toward par remained unresolved
Multi-year reinsurance tail: insurance_observer's warning that chasing excess carriers after primary disclaimers would take 3-5 years was noted but not factored into settlement timing
downstream_risk_variables: Carrier disclaimer timing: if Allen/Homburger carriers disclaim in writing before Friday, cross-claims become multi-year E&O litigation while AT1 market reprices downward
Market confidence feedback loop: immediate cross-claim filing signals adviser liability uncertainty, potentially triggering 40-60 bps repricing before any settlement clarity emerges
Reinsurance accumulation: if primary carriers disclaim on retroactive-act carve-outs, excess and reinsurance layers face 3-5 year coverage disputes while defense costs accumulate
FINMA regulatory legitimacy: aggressive litigation despite FINMA's pari passu commitment undermines regulatory authority and may harden FINMA's defense posture
Resolution distribution framework: side settlements with carriers outside resolution may create precedent conflicts with pari passu language for future AT1 claims
uncertainty_notes: The room locked in aggressive litigation (cross-claims filed, 48-hour carrier ultimatum) but left critical uncertainties unresolved: (1) whether carriers will engage in settlement talks or formalize disclaimers before Friday deadline, (2) whether FINMA's pari passu language will actually stabilize legacy AT1 pricing or merely manage litigation tail while market reprices permanently downward, (3) whether filing cross-claims before carrier settlement window closes will trigger immediate market repricing that outweighs any eventual recovery, (4) how reinsurance layers will respond if primaries disclaim on retroactive-act carve-outs, creating multi-year tail.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Cross-claims filed against adviser carriers with 48-hour ultimatum; Monday co-defendant naming threatened; tri-jurisdictional coordination locked; litigation dominated every round and drove final action
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: Room challenged March ordinance's retroactive viability trigger as violating statutory amendment procedure; demanded FINMA bracket it as Article 36 emergency-only; but accepted FINMA's emergency authority as legally defensible
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion (equity preserved, AT1 wiped) surfaced repeatedly as precedent concern and market confidence driver, but was not the primary litigation hook—room focused more on adviser liability and carrier exposure
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: Credit_market_analyst repeatedly warned of 40-120 bps permanent repricing and AT1 issuance freeze; institutional_investor demanded clarity to prevent market collapse; but litigation strategy proceeded despite these warnings
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Multi-year E&O litigation tail against advisers and carriers became central organizing theme; insurance_observer detailed 3-5 year reinsurance disputes; coverage inquiry letters sent; cross-claims filed to force immediate disclosure
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O/E&O carrier exposure (Allen, Homburger) drove tactical decisions in every round; retroactive-act carve-outs, coverage stacks, reinsurance treaties, and settlement ultimatums were core to litigation strategy and room's final actions
